ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The ethylene precursor substance ACC can generate ethylene under the action of the oxidase ACO, while acetyltransferase B (NatB) promotes the acetylation of ACO, thereby affecting the degradation rate of ACO. It is known that ethylene content is related to the bending angle of the apex of Arabidopsis seedlings. To explore the mechanism by which NatB regulates plant ethylene synthesis, researchers carried out related experiments, and the results are shown in the figure. Question: Will mutation of the NatB gene cause the endogenous ethylene level in Arabidopsis to rise or fall?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The ethylene precursor substance ACC can generate ethylene under the action of the oxidase ACO, while acetyltransferase B (NatB) promotes the acetylation of ACO, thereby affecting the degradation rate of ACO. It is known that ethylene content is related to the bending angle of the apex of Arabidopsis seedlings. To explore the mechanism by which NatB regulates plant ethylene synthesis, researchers carried out related experiments, and the results are shown in the figure. Question: Will mutation of the NatB gene cause the endogenous ethylene level in Arabidopsis to rise or fall?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the vertical axis is “apical bending angle (°)”, and the legend shows that the white bars are air treatment and the black bars are ethylene treatment. Under air treatment, the apical bending angle of wild-type seedlings is relatively large, about above 130°; the bending angle of the NatB mutant is lower than that of the wild type, about 110°; the ethylene-insensitive strain is the lowest, about 40°. Under ethylene treatment, the bending angles of both the wild type and the NatB mutant increase to relatively large and similar levels, about 160°; the ethylene-insensitive strain still maintains a relatively low angle, about 40°. Then reason: The question stem states that ethylene content is related to the apical bending angle of Arabidopsis seedlings. Under air treatment, the bending angle of the NatB mutant is lower than that of the wild type, indicating that its endogenous ethylene action effect is weaker; but after exogenous ethylene treatment, the NatB mutant can recover to a bending angle similar to that of the wild type, indicating that its ethylene perception and response abilities are basically normal. Therefore, the decrease in bending angle under air treatment should mainly be attributed to insufficient endogenous ethylene synthesis. So mutation of the NatB gene will cause the endogenous ethylene level in Arabidopsis to decrease.
